## Why This Is Asked
Assesses ability to assemble a basic yet compliant Azure OpenAI workflow with gating, logging, and versioned prompts. 

## Key Concepts
- Azure OpenAI Service behind API Management
- Azure Functions orchestration
- versioned prompts in Azure Blob
- PII redaction and content-filter guardrails
- end-to-end testing and monitoring

## Code Example
```javascript
function redactPII(text) {
  return text
    .replace(/\b[A-Z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Z0-9.-]+\.[A-Z]{2,}\b/gi, "[REDACTED_EMAIL]")
    .replace(/\b\d{3}[-.\s]?\d{3}[-.\s]?\d{4}\b/g, "[REDACTED_PHONE]");
}
```

```javascript
function postFilter(text) {
  const blocked = /\b(badword1|badword2|disallowedTopic)\b/i;
  return blocked.test(text) ? "[REDACTED_CONTENT]" : text;
}
```

- How would you test the post-filter against edge cases and false positives?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests end-to-end Azure OpenAI integration in a security context, emphasizing tenant isolation, consent gating, PII handling, auditable logs, and cost controls.

- Per-tenant isolation and consent gating
- PII redaction with Text Analytics
- End-to-end data path across Defender/Sentinel → API Management → KB grounding → OpenAI → Data Lake
- Budget-based gating per tenant for OpenAI calls
- Grounding with a versioned KB in Blob and indexing via Cognitive Search
- Offline fallback to static playbooks

## Code Example

```javascript
// Simple redaction stub for sensitive fields in alerts
function redactPII(input) {
  return input
    .replace(/(password|token|secret)\s*[:=]\s*"?[^\s"']+"?/gi, '***REDACTED***')
    .replace(/\b(api_key|credential|password_phrase)\b/gi, '***REDACTED***');
}
```
